name: Southern Ocean Surf Reef ("Midds Reef"), Middleton Beach, Albany WA
status: DERIVED: every number in "global", "lines" and "extra_layers" is computed by the script from the published 3D-model data (no new measurement); the model inputs and their sources are in "key_inputs" and in the model METHODS_3D.md.

version.name: Bluecoast final design, outer contour (design stage, volume on 2017 bathymetry)
version.date: design stage, before the March - June 2025 rock placement

frame: x alongshore (+ toward NNE, bearing 30.26 deg T); y offshore (+ toward ESE, bearing 120.26 deg T); origin = foot of the perpendicular from the traced reef centroid onto the beach-face line (edge of bright dry sand, Esri 2026-01-20)
datum: z = metres above AHD, taken as MSL (assumption A2); LAT = -0.74 m AHD (derived: LAT + mean of 2024 predicted extremes), MHHW = +0.34, MLLW = -0.26 (City of Albany crest statement)
shoreline_definition: y = 0 is the beach-face line (edge of bright dry sand) of the Esri 2026-01-20 image, NOT the MSL line. The modelled seabed (seabed.profile: z = +1.0 m at y -30, -0.5 m at y +7) crosses z = 0 (AHD = MSL) about 5 m LANDWARD of y = 0 (y_msl_crossing_m, interpolated).
units: metres; offshore_m = model y (distance from the model shoreline y = 0, positive offshore); elevations in metres above MSL (z up); x = alongshore model axis

method.reef_surface: model.js versions[design_bluecoast].grid.h_cm_b64 = reef HEIGHT above the seabed (int16 cm, 1 m cells); z = seabed(x, y) + h with the bilinear 5 m seabed (index.html buildReef: z = seaAt(x,y) + h). Height rule (build_3d.py reef_grid): crest ridge 9 m inside the steep shoreward edge, -1.0 m AHD at the offshore (east) end and -2.0 m AHD along the rest (City design table), flanks fall to the seabed with shape exponent N = 2.734, volume fitted to the stated 34,000 m3.
method.seabed: model.js seabed.profile (17 knots y -> z AHD=MSL, linearly interpolated; the 5 m seabed.z grid reproduces it within 0.04 m): medians of the RHDHV 2015 design-report contour crossings over 10 shore-normal transects (nodes -1 to -7 m), deeper nodes adjusted by eye, landward of -0.5 m and seaward of -7 m ASSUMED (build_3d.py PROFILE, A4/A5). Alongshore-UNIFORM (no x dependence). LOW confidence.

sampling.interpolation: seabed: bilinear on the model grid / analytic profile; reef surface: NaN-aware (normalised) bilinear on the reef grid; profiles at constant model x
sampling.footprint_rule: a reef cell belongs to the footprint if (reef surface - natural seabed) >= 0.10 m (ASSUMPTION, avoids zero-thickness tapers)
sampling.crest_line: x of the shallowest reef-surface cell -- OVERRIDDEN for this reef by a per-reef SURF CUT (CUT_OVERRIDES, Lior 2026-10-19); definition and reason in lines.crest_line.definition / .override; the automatic line is lines.crest_line_auto
sampling.crest_zone: contiguous points on the line within 0.10 m of the line maximum (ASSUMPTION)
sampling.ramp: seaward ramp = from the seaward edge of the crest zone to the seaward end of the reef run (the toe); ramp_length = horizontal distance, ramp_rise = reef-surface drop over it, mean_seaward_slope = rise/length
sampling.max_seaward_slope: maximum over the ramp of (z[y-1 m] - z[y+1 m]) / 2 m (central difference, 2 m baseline), tan, degrees and 1:n
sampling.toe: seaward toe = most offshore point of the reef run (reef surface still >= 0.10 m above the seabed); the reef elevation, seabed elevation and thickness there are reported (thickness > 0.5 m means the model surface is cut at its outline, not at the seabed)
sampling.gap_bridging: gaps up to 12 m along a line are bridged when forming the reef run (ASSUMPTION; only Narrowneck is affected)
sampling.alongshore_length: span = x_max - x_min of footprint cells with reef surface >= level; union = number of x-columns containing such a cell * dx. Two levels are reported because "crest -0.5 m" is ambiguous: (a) z >= -0.5 m MSL and (b) z >= crest - 0.5 m
sampling.offshore_distance: offshore_m is measured from the model shoreline y = 0 (definition in shoreline_definition); offshore_from_msl_line_m uses the first downward crossing of z = 0 (MSL) of the modelled natural seabed on the same line

caveats: 3D confidence is LOW: the plan outline is high-confidence and the crest levels are City DESIGN values, but the seabed under the reef (hence heights and flank slopes) is read from 2015 design contours; the reef shape between toe and ridge is a fitted rule (exponent N) not a survey.
Default version is the Bluecoast design outline (13,104 m2); the visible-reef version (Esri 2026-01-20) has 10,919 m2.
Slopes of the flanks follow from the fitted exponent and the volume fit to 34,000 m3 (design) and are therefore model results, not measurements.

centreline.definition: cross-shore line (constant model x) at the alongshore mid-point of the reef footprint bounding box

crest_line.definition: SURF CUT (per-reef override of the automatic crest line): cross-shore line through (x 17.0, y 118.0) m, along the model y axis (perpendicular to the shoreline). Reason: Lior 2026-10-19: the automatic crest line (x = 48 m, through the -1.0 m AHD take-off plateau at the offshore end) lies on the short offshore part of the reef, not where the wave is ridden. The cut is moved to the middle of the long -2.0 m AHD ridge ("crest 110 m @ -2 m AHD", City of Albany / Bluecoast design table, SOURCE_AUDIT_2026-10-10 design_table): the ridge cells of the model (row-wise maximum of the reef surface, z > -2.15 m) run from (x 3, y 68) to (x 38, y 168); the middle of that -2 m ridge is about (x 17, y 118). Cut perpendicular to the shoreline (model x = 17 m constant; the Albany frame is shore-normal). Built reef is a left-hander with the take-off at the offshore (east) end and the ride along this ridge (design table "left-hander, peel 60 deg, rides to 100 m"; 07_scale/shapes/southern-ocean-surf-reef-albany/HANDOFF.md, 3d/REGISTER_3D.md A7).

override.reason: Lior 2026-10-19: the automatic crest line (x = 48 m, through the -1.0 m AHD take-off plateau at the offshore end) lies on the short offshore part of the reef, not where the wave is ridden. The cut is moved to the middle of the long -2.0 m AHD ridge ("crest 110 m @ -2 m AHD", City of Albany / Bluecoast design table, SOURCE_AUDIT_2026-10-10 design_table): the ridge cells of the model (row-wise maximum of the reef surface, z > -2.15 m) run from (x 3, y 68) to (x 38, y 168); the middle of that -2 m ridge is about (x 17, y 118). Cut perpendicular to the shoreline (model x = 17 m constant; the Albany frame is shore-normal). Built reef is a left-hander with the take-off at the offshore (east) end and the ride along this ridge (design table "left-hander, peel 60 deg, rides to 100 m"; 07_scale/shapes/southern-ocean-surf-reef-albany/HANDOFF.md, 3d/REGISTER_3D.md A7).

second_crest_line.definition: cross-shore line through the shallowest reef cell on the OTHER side of the centreline than the main crest line (for two-arm reefs: the other arm); crest cell z = -2.03 m MSL

crest_line_auto.definition: cross-shore line (constant model x) through the shallowest crest cell of the reef surface (ties within 0.02 m: the cell nearest the middle of the shallowest plateau) [AUTOMATIC RULE, superseded for this reef by the override in crest_line; kept for reference, not used downstream]

reconstruction_check.what: volume of the reef grid read here (sum of max(reef - seabed, 0) over all finite reef cells, no thickness threshold, seabed from this script) against the volume stated by the model for the same version; a check that the surface was reconstructed as the viewer draws it
reconstruction_check.stated_source: model.js versions[design_bluecoast].volume_m3 (fitted to the stated 34,000 m3)
